origin: assistant-authored synthetic draft; not human reviewed

episode.beginning: The user moved their workshop to Cedar Street in March.

expected_units.content: The user moved their workshop to Cedar Street in March.
expected_units.rationale: An event with stated time, not an immutable trait.

cases.annotation_notes: Do not infer the user enjoys woodworking or will remain at this address forever.

episode.beginning: The user is choosing a weekly report format.
episode.middle: The user says: "I prefer a short written summary because I can read it between meetings."

expected_units.content: The user prefers a short written weekly report because they can read it between meetings.
expected_units.rationale: The supplied reason belongs to the preference, not an invented user trait.

cases.annotation_notes: Retain the report scope and rationale together; do not infer a general aversion to detail.

episode.beginning: Last month the user said they preferred morning planning sessions.
episode.middle: Today the user says: "Please schedule planning in the afternoon now; my morning shift changed."

expected_units.content: Last month the user preferred morning planning sessions.
The user now prefers afternoon planning sessions because their morning shift changed.
expected_units.rationale: Changed current preference, qualified by now; independent from historical state.

cases.annotation_notes: Reviewer must settle historical-label inclusion before capture. Do not collapse opposing preferences into a timeless trait.

episode.beginning: The user chose a train over a flight after two cancellations.
episode.middle: The user says: "For my short trips with fixed arrival deadlines, I will choose the option with a backup departure rather than the lowest fare."

expected_units.content: After two cancellations, the user chose a train instead of a flight.
For short trips with fixed arrival deadlines, the user will prioritize a backup departure over the lowest fare.
expected_units.rationale: Explicit user-specific future decision principle grounded in the failed alternatives.

cases.annotation_notes: Do not replace the insight with generic travel advice or invent a fear of flying.

episode.beginning: At one team lunch, the user ordered a vegetarian soup.
episode.middle: No reason or longer-term food preference was discussed.

expected_units.content: The user ordered a vegetarian soup at one team lunch.
expected_units.rationale: One observed choice does not establish vegetarianism.

cases.annotation_notes: Reject vegetarian identity, permanent diet restrictions and health explanations as unsupported.
Courtesy-only exchange: no durable memory is proposed. This is a draft judgment awaiting human review.

episode.beginning: The user has a blue bicycle and a red toolbox.
episode.middle: The toolbox is kept in the hallway.

expected_units.content: The user has a blue bicycle.
The user has a red toolbox.
The toolbox is kept in the hallway.
expected_units.rationale: Location can change independently of ownership/color.

cases.annotation_notes: Reviewer should decide whether color and ownership merit further splitting; freeze that decision consistently.

episode.beginning: The user is discussing how to compare unfamiliar software.
episode.middle: The user says: "For my evaluations, I choose the tool with a reversible trial because it lets me change course after testing."

expected_units.content: For unfamiliar-software evaluations, the user chooses a reversible trial so they can change course after testing.
expected_units.rationale: An explicit contextual preference with rationale can also support a user-specific decision principle.

cases.annotation_notes: Allow either annotated type, count the unit once, and do not reward duplicate cross-type paraphrases.
